question.text: Raima Equities defended its lack of PEP identification system by claiming that clients were "known persons" introduced by directors/shareholders. How did the Adjudicating Officer (AO) view this defense?

answer.text: The AO did not find any merit in this submission and concluded that no PEP identification system existed
The AO accepted this as a valid PEP identification method
The AO recommended this approach for all small brokers
The AO suspended the case pending further investigation

explanation.text: The Logic: Raima Equities submitted that its clients were introduced by directors, shareholders and sub-brokers and were therefore "known persons", and on that basis no separate PEP identification system was needed. The Adjudicating Officer did not find any merit in this submission and concluded that the entity did not have a system to identify Politically Exposed Persons. The Trap: Knowing clients informally through directors, shareholders or sub-brokers does not, by itself, amount to a PEP identification system in the AO's view. The defense of "known persons" was specifically rejected. Note: The AO's rejection of the known-persons defense in the Raima Equities matter is set out on pages 112-113 of the NISM Series XXIV AML and CFT Provisions in Securities Markets Certification Examination Workbook (November 2025).
